title: Route Economics Resolver — deterministic per-route/model/customer cost & latency attribution
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements the Route Economics Resolver: a deterministic attribution service that computes per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns consumed by the Console and billing/insights pipelines. The goal is explainable, stable numbers that match billing cadence while being useful for realtime ops and root-cause analysis.

Motivation and background:
- Current console views show aggregated unit economics but lack a single source-of-truth mapping from incoming API requests -> model execution -> infra amortization -> per-customer cost.
- We need consistent attributions for: the Console Cost Explorer, per-route throttling heuristics, and cost alerts (usage spikes).
- Differentiator: make the attribution deterministic and auditable (row-level provenance) so PMs/customer success can explain spikes and reconcile with invoices.

Design overview (decisions so far):
1) Two-stage model: (A) lightweight real-time resolver that emits per-request raw contributions to a Kafka topic; (B) a daily materialized reconcile job (Materialize/SQL) that consumes the stream + infra cost allocations and produces the final per-route/model/cust summaries.
2) Attribution granularity: token-level costing for generation requests (open-loop): cost(request) = sum(token_steps_model_variant_cost) + proportional share of shared infra (autoscaler, reserved GPU idle time) amortized by token-weighted usage window. For embeddings and fast paths, attribution will use per-request samples and a deterministic estimator to avoid heavy compute.
3) Latency decomposition: split into client->edge, queue-wait, model-compute, post-processing. Edge/queue measured from ingress traces; model-compute from serving runtime telemetry (start/stop per-request). We will surface p50/p95/p99 and mean for each decomposition.
4) Determinism and explainability: resolver attaches a compact provenance blob (route, model_version, kernel_profile, batch_id, kv_cache_hit_ratio_estimate) to every emitted record so downstream viewers can reconstruct how numbers were computed.
5) Streaming infra: use an independent consumer group on the existing "inference-observability" Kafka topic namespace. The resolver will be a horizontally-scaled Flink job (event-time processing) with exactly-once semantics writing to the "route-econ-raw-v1" topic. Materialize will create incremental views for console queries and daily reconciled exports (parquet) for billing/backfill.

Open trade-offs and unresolved questions:
- Cost of token-level attribution vs CPU/GPU overhead in the serving runtime: we chose lightweight telemetry hooks (emit per-request summary with token_count + model_variant_cost_rate) rather than instrumenting each kernel call to keep production overhead low. Trade-off: slightly coarser compute cost estimate but much lower perf impact.
- Shared infra amortization window: 1-day window gives stability but delays surfacing true short spikes. Plan: smoothing with a 1-hour anomaly tag plus 24h amortization for final numbers.
- Realtime vs eventual: console will show provisional realtime numbers (low-latency estimator) and a reconciled daily number flagged as "final".

Acceptance criteria (must pass for PR):
- Resolver job emits records for >=99.9% of incoming inference requests for a 24h test window in staging (no more than 0.1% missing).
- Materialized views compute per-route/model/customer cost and latency with documented formulas; sample spot-checks reconcile to billing rolls within 2% for synthetic workload tests.
- Console cost explorer displays per-route and per-model rows with breakdown columns: compute_cost, infra_amortization, kv_cache_savings, network_cost, p50_latency_decomp, p95_latency_decomp.
- Each emitted raw record includes a provenance blob and a deterministic hash that maps to the summarized row for easy tracing.
- Test coverage: unit tests for attribution math, e2e integration test that runs in staging (synthetic load) and verifies topology end-to-end.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1 (spike): prototype resolver logic in a Flink job reading existing telemetry topic; define record schema and provenance blob. (owner: Liam)
- Week 2: integrate runtime telemetry hooks (lightweight hook emitting request-summaries). Deploy to canary region with sampling=100% in staging. (owner: runtime infra)
- Week 3: wire Materialize views + console API endpoints; create provisional console UI rows using realtime estimator. (owner: Observability backend)
- Week 4: run 48h synthetic workload, reconcile, iterate on amortization parameters, add anomaly tagging. Prepare rollout plan for prod.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary in one region behind a feature flag (console.feature.route_econ_resolver=true). Start with 10% sampled production traffic for 48h, compare to existing aggregated metrics.
- Expand sampling and run reconciliation daily for two weeks before marking numbers as primary in Console.
- Post-deploy: add an ops dashboard showing resolver throughput, lag, and missing-counts; create alerts for >1% unresolved mapping.

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing consumers (billing and console) will keep using their current rollups until the reconciled view is validated. We will publish a migration mapping doc.
- Schema versioning: resolver messages use a top-level "schema_version" field; Materialize views are built off schema_version=v1. We will support migration to v2 with a CompatibilityTransformer job.

Review feedback and follow-ups (from initial design review on 2026-02-28):
- PM (R. Chen): requested clearer UX labeling for provisional vs reconciled numbers — added to acceptance criteria.
- Security (J. Patel): asked to confirm that provenance blob does not contain PII; we agreed to hash any customer-identifying strings and keep raw ids in an access-controlled table.
- Infra (K. Nguyen): recommended Materialize for low-latency incremental views; noted we need a retention plan for topics. Action: add TTL policy to route-econ-raw-v1 (30d).

- Check that the proposed streaming topology aligns with existing Kafka topic ownership and capacity limits.
